findings.title: Sudoers rule gives the operator account effective root
findings.description:
`MT_INSTALL` allows root to run `/home/manta/source/repos/manta/trading-data/deploy/install-production.sh --ref *`. That script lives in a checkout owned by `manta`, so `manta` can edit it and then run it as root. That makes the rule full root, which contradicts the file header ("nothing wider").

The other wildcards are loose too:
- `systemctl stop|start|restart|is-active mt-*` also accepts extra arguments after the unit name, because sudoers `*` matches spaces.
- `/usr/local/bin/mt-run *` passes arbitrary arguments to a root-run wrapper. I did not check what `mt-run` does with them.

Install the script to a root-owned path, for example the already-installed copy under `/opt`. Then list the exact argument forms, with no trailing `*`, or validate `--ref` inside the script.

`MT_READ` exposes `/etc/manta-trading.env`, which holds secrets. Document that on purpose, or have the scripts read only the specific variables they need.

findings.title: Cagg freshness probe can be wrong in both directions and is only tested with mocks
findings.description:
Three problems:
1. It compares `last_successful_finish` with `max(created_at)`. A refresh that started before a bar was written and finished after it passes as fresh, although it did not materialize that bar. `last_run_started_at`, or the refresh start of the last successful run, is the correct comparison.
2. A refresh policy's `end_offset` can exclude the newest buckets from materialization entirely. The probe never accounts for that, so it can report fresh when the cagg still lacks the data.
3. The join filters `job.hypertable_name = %s` using the cagg name. I could not confirm that `timescaledb_information.jobs` reports a cagg policy under the cagg's name rather than its internal materialization hypertable. If it does not, the query returns no row and `last_refresh` is `None`. Every verify then returns `[WAIT]` whenever bars exist, and the cutover can never reach COMPLETE.

The unit tests mock the cursor and only check that the SQL text contains certain strings. Add an integration test against a real Timescale database that uses a throwaway DB created by the fixture.

findings.title: Import ordering will fail the required ruff `I` rule
findings.description:
Several import blocks are not sorted:
- `cutover_921_minute_sessions.py` has `NOTES_DIR, fire_unit_until, start_log` ahead of `CutoverError, fire_unit, ...`.
- `repair_921_minute_sessions.py` and `test_repair_921.py` import `cagg_freshness_for_session` ahead of `CheckReport` and `SymbolFindings`.
- `minute.py` inserts `daemon.minute_sessions` and `gaps.*` imports out of order relative to the existing `data.gaps` block.

Run `ruff check --select I --fix` and `ruff format`.

findings.title: Verify polling treats an unlocatable refresh as a transient wait
findings.description: The loop sleeps up to 5×15 minutes, then returns the last `[WAIT]` text. The caller treats this as INCOMPLETE with the message "read the FAIL lines", but a WAIT result contains no FAIL line. Make the final message say "verify still waiting for cagg refresh" so the operator knows what happened. Also log the `[WAIT]` text itself in the narration file, not just the poll counter.

findings.title: Session-level judgement drops the weekend tolerance
findings.description:
The new logic is sound, and the chunk-by-session tests cover the spillover case. Two behavioral consequences are worth knowing about:
- A session the provider never publishes, such as a halted day, stays PARTIAL forever. The gap row is kept and `attempt_count` climbs.
- `judge_chunk_by_sessions` builds `judged` and then `sessions_without_bars` recomputes the same filter, which is a small duplication.

`_UTC = UTC` is a redundant alias.

findings.title: Test setup duplicated across the new daemon tests
findings.description: `TestChunkJudgedBySessions._run` and `test_last_bar_before_the_chunk_end_is_still_success` repeat roughly 40 lines of identical mock setup. The second test could reuse `_run` if `_run` took bounds and the gap end as parameters. Extract a fixture or helper.

findings.title: Logging in the cutover helpers is split between `say` and `print`
findings.description: `say` tees to the log file, but `wait_for_unit_or_line`, `fire_unit_until` and `fire_unit` write their progress with bare `print`. The file therefore misses those lines. `_LOG_FILE` is also module-global state. `start_log` truncates any existing file at the same path, which is only safe because the path includes a timestamp.

findings.title: Timer comment may be stale
findings.description: I did not verify this. The comment says the minute pass is "Staggered 30 minutes behind mt-daily-pass.timer". With the firing moved from 01:05 to 04:05, that offset may no longer hold. Check it against `mt-daily-pass.timer`.

findings.title: Time-of-day constant and its dependents move together
findings.description: `MINUTE_PASS_FIRING_TIMES_UTC`, the timer file, the docstrings and the health and constants tests were all updated consistently to 04:05 and 07:05. The UTC formatting fix in `check_minute_session_mass` is correct.
